memories.content: The user stores prepared meals on the second shelf of the freezer.
The user went to the market without a shopping list and bought onions that were already at home.
On a day the user shopped after checking a refrigerator photo, they did not make a duplicate purchase.
On a day the user made a spicy stew, they left part of one bowl uneaten.
The next time the user cooked it, they used half as much chili powder and finished the meal.
When cooking with their younger brother, the user assigned the cooking sequence only verbally and they did the same task twice.
The next time, the user and their younger brother split ingredient preparation and heat control and finished the meal 20 minutes earlier.
When cooking together, the user's younger brother prefers to divide the cooking and dishwashing roles in advance.
The local agent can compare responses across several meals, but it cannot conclude from one unfinished food item that the user dislikes that ingredient.
The condition of frozen prepared food may vary with its packaging and storage duration.
The user collects clothes for donation in a large bag beside the entrance.
After emptying an entire drawer at once, the user could not find a charger they needed.
During the next organizing session, the user sorted items by type and put only items to be discarded in the bag.
Even after photographing unworn clothes, the user did not take them out again for one month.
After moving those clothes to the donation bag, the user cleared one closet compartment.
The user nearly discarded an important paper with advertising and checked the recycling box again.
During the next organizing session, the user kept a separate document box and did not mix the papers.
The user's mother asks the user to check whether she needs kitchen items in good condition before discarding them.
Confirm with the user before marking a personal document or another person's property as a disposal candidate.
The local agent cannot determine an object's emotional meaning from frequency of use alone.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate household domains: food storage, shopping, cooking, and meal interpretation versus decluttering, donation, document handling, and disposal safeguards. Their only substantive overlap is a shared caution against inferring latent attitudes from limited behavior, with each frame preserving a different application scope.

relations.reason: The food claim concerns inferring ingredient dislike from one unfinished item, whereas the organizing claim concerns inferring emotional meaning from frequency of use; these explicit scopes must be preserved.
relations.summary: Both frames restrict the local agent from inferring a latent attitude solely from limited behavioral evidence, under different domains and evidence patterns.

relations.reason: This food-storage location is independently useful and has no substantively corresponding claim in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Prepared meals are stored on the freezer’s second shelf.

relations.reason: The paired observations express one reference-only claim about inventory awareness and duplicate purchasing, with no counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Checking a refrigerator photo before shopping is associated with avoiding the duplicate purchase experienced when shopping without a list.

relations.reason: These observations form one reference-only account of a recipe adjustment and changed meal outcome, absent from the compared frame.
relations.summary: After leaving part of a spicy stew uneaten, the user halved the chili powder on the next attempt and finished the meal.

relations.reason: The memories split one reference-only claim about improving coordination with the younger brother, with no corresponding compared-side claim.
relations.summary: Replacing verbal-only sequencing with divided preparation and heat-control responsibilities avoided duplicated work and shortened shared cooking.

relations.reason: This specific collaboration preference is independently useful and is not addressed by the compared frame.
relations.summary: The younger brother prefers cooking and dishwashing roles to be divided before cooking together.

relations.reason: This qualification about frozen-food condition has no substantively matching compared-side information.
relations.summary: Packaging and storage duration may affect the condition of frozen prepared food.

relations.reason: This organizing location and purpose appear only in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Clothes intended for donation are collected in a large bag beside the entrance.

relations.reason: The memories form one compared-only account of changing the organizing method after a retrieval problem, without a reference-side counterpart.
relations.summary: After losing track of a needed charger when emptying a whole drawer, the user later sorted by type and bagged only discard items.

relations.reason: These observations split one compared-only claim about acting on persistently unused clothes and the resulting space gain.
relations.summary: Photographing unworn clothes did not prompt reuse, while moving them to the donation bag cleared closet space.

relations.reason: The memories express one compared-only document-sorting safeguard and its motivating incident.
relations.summary: After nearly discarding an important paper with advertising, the user used a separate document box and avoided mixing papers.

relations.reason: This family-specific reuse check is independently useful and has no reference-side counterpart.
relations.summary: The user’s mother asks to be consulted about whether she needs usable kitchen items before they are discarded.

relations.reason: This disposal-confirmation policy for sensitive or externally owned items appears only in the compared frame.
relations.summary: The agent should confirm with the user before marking personal documents or another person’s property as disposal candidates.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame uniquely covers donation storage, staged sorting, moving unused clothes, separating documents, checking family reuse needs, and obtaining confirmation before treating sensitive or others’ property as disposable.
reports.differences: Both limit behavioral inference, but one concerns ingredient dislike after an unfinished serving while the other concerns emotional meaning inferred from use frequency.
reports.reference_only: The reference uniquely records freezer practices, duplicate-shopping prevention, spice adjustment, shared-cooking coordination, the brother’s role preference, and packaging or duration effects on frozen food.
